rows.endpoint: none: a statement before a spend
rows.what: Stated before the spend (change note 004 item 7): one pass of lines 1 to 9
rows.answer: One pass of the script's 12 pieces (lines 1 to 9: 146 words, 37 pause marks, 1,647 characters sent) is about 549 credits. Worked out from this ledger's own 45 narrator calls with pause marks: 0.4518 a character of words and 4.098 a pause mark, worst miss 0.64 a call. That leaves about 101 of the cap of 650 for single lines done again. The check this tool makes before a call counts every sent character at 0.439 and so reads high: 728 for the pass.

rows.endpoint: none: a statement before a spend
rows.what: narration: line 9 done again with a longer pause
rows.answer: line.decision.reset.0 take 1 reads at 1.617 words a second against the limit of 1.6, so it cannot be kept. One take more with its pause asked at 1.3 s in place of 1.0 s: about 17 credits. Narration cap then about 563 of 650.

rows.endpoint: none: a statement before a spend
rows.what: narration: line 1 done again without pause marks, at the voice's saved settings
rows.answer: Brandon, in the Builder's chat about 10:50 PM MT November 27: the voiceover has huge pauses throughout the sentences, which he did not intend, and the voice is way too deep and does not sound right. MEASURED: every take was sent at speed 0.7 with a break mark at each pause mark; on the same test line the voice sits at a middle pitch of 111 to 120 Hz at its saved speed 1.0 and at 76 to 80 Hz in three of four takes at speed 0.7; the kept line 1 sits at 71 Hz with 8.3 s of silence in 19.5 s. One take of line 1 (line.marketing.stroll.0), 125 characters, no pause mark, no setting sent so the voice's saved settings apply (speed 1.0, stability 0.5, similarity 0.75, style 0): about 57 credits at this ledger's 0.4518 a character. Narration cap then about 620 of 650. The other eleven pieces wait for his word: they do not fit under the cap.

rows.what: sound effects, first pass, change notes 002 to 004: the cost before the spend
rows.answer: Stated before the spend (change note 004 item 7). The first pass of the sound effects for change notes 002 to 004: one take each of 32 sounds, expected cost 296 credits at the measured 11 a second with the service's least length of 0.5 s (this tool's own check counts 12 a second: 319). The ledger stands at 3784 before; expected after, about 4080; under the effects cap 0 of 700 before, about 296 after. Until Partner brings the answer on the caps no more than 360 is spent on effects. In order, id and seconds asked: named by change note 002: turret-cannon 0.8 (the step 1 turret's shot, in place of the toy laser), slab-slam 1.0, keys-break 0.6, button-burst 1.2, big-fire 1.5 (the boss's great blast, today on a stand-in of 0.5 s). Key events: pin-bumper 0.5, pin-target 0.5, pin-bell 0.5, pin-kick 0.5, pin-coins 0.9, pin-frenzy 2.4, vacuum-roar 3.0 (loop), vacuum-gulp 0.5, vacuum-slip 0.5, cannon-fire 0.5, cannon-tell 0.8, boss-heal 0.6, shield-glance 0.5, arena-split 0.6, arena-rise 0.9, healthbar-drop 0.5, power-up 0.8, boss-fall 0.8, pillar-break 0.8. Secondary: reel-stop 0.5, stop-press 0.5, date-miss 0.6, volume-sign 0.5, row-close 0.5, folder-open 0.5, slot-in 0.5, wind-gust 1.2. Every prompt ends with the kit's line word for word. Held for later: the finish's own sounds (they wait for the camera's marks; about 61 for the five that matter most), file-pick, and the six the list marks as first to cut or able to share a file. No second take is made before every sound has its first.
